Then: **every** bounded smooth function $\psi:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C$ that solves the free time-independent Schrödinger equation $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi=E\psi$ pointwise determines a pure preparation of the model with position density $|\psi|^{2}$; in particular the plane wave $\psi_{k}(x)=e^{ik\cdot x}$ with $k\ne0$ is a preparation with constant position density $|\psi_{k}|^{2}=1$, and the point-localized object $\delta^{3}(x-X)$ is the preparation of a particle exactly at $X$.

$H_{V}=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V}$ is self-adjoint with domain

clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]]
clause (a)).

generator_paragraphs:
**(b) Orbital angular momentum.** For $i=1,2,3$ let $L_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint operator on $H_{s}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]], the Stone
generator of the coordinate rotation group $t\mapsto U(R_{i}(t))$, so that
$U(R_{i}(t))=e^{-itL_{i}/\hbar}$ and, on the Schwartz class,
$$L_{i}\psi=\sum_{j,k=1}^{3}\varepsilon_{ijk}\,Q_{j}P_{k}\psi$$
([[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] clause (b),
[[def-strongly-continuous-one-parameter-unitary-group]]). The model reads
$(L_{i},\mathrm{J\,s})$ as an **assigned sharp observable**, called the
$i$-th **orbital angular momentum** of the model, with outcome law
$\mu^{L_{i}}_{\rho}$ in a preparation $\rho$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a),(b),
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). The operators
$L_{i}$ act on the spatial factor only; their reading on the angular degrees
of freedom is the one supplied by the sphere operators
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-orbital-self-adjoint-generators]] and
[[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-onb]], and the finite-blocks identity
$\sum_{i}L_{i}^{2}F=\hbar^{2}l(l+1)F$ on the harmonic span is the content of a
separate lemma of this page
([[lem-nrqm-angular-momentum-orbital-casimir-identity]]).

items.use_anchor:
**(c) The assigned energy operator.** Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary
Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), $c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let
$$H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}):=\bigl\{f\in H_{0}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{0}\bigr\}$$
be the free operator of that clause with $d=3$ and $b=0$. With $M_{V}$ the
bounded multiplication operator of clause (a) of the same theorem, the
**assigned energy operator** of the model with central potential $V$ is
$$H_{V}:=H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V}):=D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{free}}).$$
The declared energy unit is the joule. By clause (c) of the cited theorem
$H_{V}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{V})$, bounded below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$; by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] the domain is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and
$$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f+Vf\qquad(f\in D(H_{V})),$$
$\Delta_{w}=D_{1}^{2}+D_{2}^{2}+D_{3}^{2}$ the weak Laplacian of that lemma, so
that on any open set on which $V$ is of class $C^{2}$ the model's
time-independent equation is the ordinary differential equation
$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi+V\psi=E\psi$ for a $C^{2}$ representative. The
model adopts $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ as its declared energy observable; its
self-adjointness is the cited theorem's, and no further spectral property is
presupposed here.

items.use_anchor:
**(e) Local instruments.** Let $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ be a
declared finite or countable instrument of subsystem $A$ with Kraus family as
in [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]
clause (d), normalized in the strong sense
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I_{H}$. The **local extension** of the instrument
to the declared composite is the family
$$\bigl(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K}\bigr)_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$$
together with the outcome effects $\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})=\bigl(\sum_{r}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$
and the conditional updates
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})\,\rho\,(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*},\qquad p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,F_{a}^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigr).$$
It is normalized: every finite partial sum of
$\sum_{a,r}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})^{*}(M_{a,r}\otimes I_{K})$ equals
$\bigl(\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}\bigr)\otimes I_{K}$ by linearity
of tensoring with $I_{K}$, the finite partial sums
$\sum_{a\le N,r\le R}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}$ are uniformly bounded by $I_{H}$ and
converge strongly to $I_{H}$, so clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-local-pvm-tensor-extension]] gives strong convergence of
the extended partial sums to $I_{H}\otimes I_{K}$; hence the local extension is
a declared finite or countable instrument of the composite in the sense of
clause (d) of
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. The
same construction applies with the roles of $A$ and $B$ exchanged.

items.use_anchor:
Adopt the framework's composition and state readings for a declared composite
of two distinguishable subsystems
([[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]]), the kinematics and
massive-particle model of P5 for a particle subsystem of spin label
$s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ with mass parameter $m>0$ and space
$H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, $r=2s+1$
([[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). In the model below the particle
subsystem is $A$ and the marker subsystem is $B$. The following vocabulary is
used by this page.
 
**(a) Position readout of the particle factor.** The model's componentwise
position family has joint spectral projection valued measure $G$ on the Borel
sets of $\mathbb R^{3}$, with
$$G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}},\qquad \mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$$
for $\psi\in H_{s}$ of unit norm and Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$, read in
the metre unit of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
([[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] clause (b),
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)). A
**declared detection bin** is a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$; the
**local position-bin effect** of the declared composite is the bounded effect
$G(B)\otimes I_{K}$ of [[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]]
clause (d), and the **detection weight** of a preparation $\rho'$ of the
composite is
$$p_{\rho'}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho'\,(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr)\in[0,1],$$
the reading of clause (iv) of P2 for that local effect.
 
**(b) Declared marked two-component model.** A **declared marked
two-component model** of the arrangement consists of: two unit vectors
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\in H_{s}$, the **path components** relative to the declared
pair of alternative path conditions; and two unit vectors $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
the **marker states** correlated with the alternatives. The assignment of
$\psi_{1},\psi_{2},e_{1},e_{2}$ and of the alternatives is declared apparatus
data in the sense of P7; it is not computed from the framework, and no element
of this definition asserts that a particle described by the model "took" one
of the two alternatives. A declared marked model is **overlap-normalized**
when $\langle\psi_{1},\psi_{2}\rangle=0$, and **trivially marked** when
$|\langle e_{1},e_{2}\rangle|=1$.
 
**(c) Phase family and marked preparations.** For $\varphi\in\mathbb R$ put
$$\Psi(\varphi):=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\Bigl(\kappa(\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1})+e^{i\varphi}\kappa(\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2})\Bigr)\in H_{s}\widehat\otimes K,$$
where $\kappa$ is the embedding of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]].
Define the **admissible phase set** $I:=\{\varphi\in\mathbb R:\Psi(\varphi)\ne0\}$. It is nonempty: $\Psi(0)+\Psi(\pi)=\sqrt2\,\kappa(\psi_1\otimes e_1)\ne0$, so those two vectors cannot both vanish, using $e^{i\pi}=-1$ from [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The **marked preparation at an admissible phase $\varphi\in I$** is the state assigned to the nonzero vector $\Psi(\varphi)$,
$$\rho(\varphi):=\widehat\rho\bigl(\Psi(\varphi)\bigr)=\frac{T_{\Psi(\varphi),\Psi(\varphi)}}{\|\Psi(\varphi)\|^{2}}\in D(H_{s}\widehat\otimes K)$$
([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] clause (c)); the phase
$\varphi$ is read in radians (dimensionless). The **marker-carried which-path
preparation** is the statistical mixture
$$\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}:=\tfrac12\,T_{\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1},\,\psi_{1}\otimes e_{1}}+\tfrac12\,T_{\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2},\,\psi_{2}\otimes e_{2}},$$
a preparation of the declared composite by clause (iii) of P1.
 
**(d) Detection weights of the family.** For a declared detection bin $B$ and admissible phase $\varphi\in I$ put
$$p(\varphi)(B):=p_{\rho(\varphi)}(B)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho(\varphi)(G(B)\otimes I_{K})\bigr),\qquad p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B):=p_{\rho_{\mathrm{mix}}}(B)=\tfrac12\bigl(\langle G(B)\psi_{1},\psi_{1}\rangle+\langle G(B)\psi_{2},\psi_{2}\rangle\bigr).$$
The numbers $p(\varphi)(B)$ and $p_{\mathrm{mix}}(B)$ lie in $[0,1]$; they are
probabilities of the declared model, not measured frequencies.
 
**(e) Fringe visibility.** The **fringe visibility of the declared phase
family at the bin $B$** is
$$V(B):=\frac{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)-\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}\qquad\text{whenever }\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)>0,$$
and is left undefined otherwise; all extrema, including the denominator, are taken over the nonempty admissible phase set $I$ of clause (c). The number $V(B)$ is a property of the declared model
and the declared bin, read as the modulation contrast of the family of
probabilities; it is not a measured visibility and carries no statement about
an apparatus.
 
**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) fix the model vocabulary. The path components,
marker states and the identification of a concrete apparatus with the declared
model are declared and tested inputs in the sense of clauses (i)-(iii) of P7;
no dynamics, no interaction, no environment, no detector response, no counts
and no empirical result is asserted. In particular the model does not claim
that the marker is measured or read out, that the alternatives are physically
realized, or that the loss of contrast described by $V$ is caused by any
particular process; the quantitative statement about $V$ is the content of a
separate theorem of this page.
items.disposition: Definition(c) uses e^{i varphi} as a phase-labelled preparation, and Definition(f) expressly asserts no dynamics. No time-group generator is transferred.

**(b) Declared species and sector.** A **declared species sector** of the model
consists of: a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$, the
**one-particle space** of the species, as assigned in P1; a mass parameter
$m>0$ in kg; a spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and the
internal factor $V_{s}=\mathbb C^{2s+1}$ of P6 clause (ii), with the
**orbital factor** $H_{\mathrm{sp}}$ the factor carrying no internal degree of
freedom when the one-particle space is given as a completed product
$H_{\mathrm{sp}}\widehat\otimes V_{s}$; for the massive spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] the one-particle space
is $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$, whose spin components are the
internal factor of P6 clause (ii) in the reading of that definition; a
**statistics choice**
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, where $+$ declares the species **bosonic** and $-$
declares it **fermionic**; and, for a charged species, a charge parameter
$q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. The parameters and the statistics choice are
empirical model assignments with their uncertainties, in the sense of P6
clause (iii); no value and no statistics choice is derived by this definition.

**(c) The assigned energy operator.** Let $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ be real,
bounded and measurable; write $\|V\|_{\infty}:=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|V(x)|$.
The **assigned energy operator** of the line model with potential $V$ is
$$H_{V}:=H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}}+M_{V},\qquad H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad c:=\frac{2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}}{m},$$
with $M_{V}$ the multiplication operator of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (a), on the common domain
$D(H_{V}):=D(H_{0}^{\mathrm{lin}})
=\{f\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}\}$,
where $\mathcal F_{2}$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a)-(c)). The declared energy unit is the joule. By
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-free-operator-differential-identification]] the domain
$D(H_{V})$ is the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and
$$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,D^{2}f+Vf\qquad(f\in D(H_{V})),$$
$D^{2}$ the second weak derivative, so the model's time-independent equation
inside any open interval on which $V$ is (say) constant is the ordinary
differential equation $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''+V\psi=E\psi$. The model
adopts $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ as its assigned energy observable in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a); its
self-adjointness is established by the line-model energy theorem of this page
and is not presupposed here. A declared potential is **compactly supported** when $V$
vanishes almost everywhere outside some bounded interval.

with probability $\tfrac12$ and $T_{e_{-},e_{-}}$ with probability $\tfrac12$,
so that
$$\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}:=\tfrac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+\tfrac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}};$$
 
(c) the **EPR-type product mixture** of the composite: the declared
preparation
$$M:=\tfrac12T_{e_{+}\otimes e_{-},\,e_{+}\otimes e_{-}}+\tfrac12T_{e_{-}\otimes e_{+},\,e_{-}\otimes e_{+}},$$
in which each factor carries a definite spin along the $z$-axis and the two
spins are opposite.
 
Then:
 
(i) $\rho_{A}=\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}=\tfrac12 I$ and the marginals of $M$ are
$\operatorname{Tr}_{B}M=\tfrac12I=\operatorname{Tr}_{A}M$: the two
preparations of factor $A$ and the marginal of $M$ are the same density
operator, and $\rho$ and $M$ are not the same composite preparation;
 
(ii) for unit directions $a,b$, writing $a_{3}=a\cdot e_{z}$ and
$b_{3}=b\cdot e_{z}$ with $e_{z}$ the direction of the $z$-axis of the basis
$(e_{+},e_{-})$, the directional correlation of the singlet is
$\mathbb E_{\rho}(a,b)=-\cos\theta=-a\cdot b$ while that of the product mixture
is
$$\mathbb E_{M}(a,b)=-\tfrac12a_{3}b_{3}-\tfrac12a_{3}b_{3}=-a_{3}b_{3};$$
in particular $\mathbb E_{\rho}(z,z)=\mathbb E_{M}(z,z)=-1$ but
$\mathbb E_{\rho}(x,x)=-1$ and $\mathbb E_{M}(x,x)=0$ for the orthogonal
direction $x$;
 
(iii) $M$ is a convex combination of the two pure product states
$T_{e_{+}\otimes e_{-},\,\cdot}$ and $T_{e_{-}\otimes e_{+},\,\cdot}$, hence a
separable preparation in the sense of clause (b) of
[[def-nrqm-composites-separable-and-entangled-states]], while $\rho$ is a
non-product pure preparation; and every local readout law of factor $A$ is
the same in $\rho$, in $\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}$ extended by any preparation of
$B$, and in $M$, because all three have the reduced preparation $\tfrac12I$ on
$A$;
 
(iv) consequently the density operator $\tfrac12I$ alone does not determine
whether the preparation of factor $A$ arises as the reduction of an entangled
composite preparation (the improper case) or from a classical randomization
of factor preparations (the proper case): the two cases are distinguished by
the joint statistics with the other factor, not by any local statistic of
$A$.
 
The comparison is a conditional computation of the declared framework; it
asserts no measured correlation, no experiment and no empirical fact.

$$K:=\frac{\sqrt{2m(E+U)}}{\hbar},\qquad k:=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},\qquad E>0 .$$

The source is the primary preprint of Bach, Pope, Liou and Batelaan
(arXiv:1210.6243v1, 22 October 2012), reporting a controlled double-slit
electron diffraction experiment. The reported apparatus consists of a
thermionic tungsten filament with electrostatic lenses producing an electron
beam of energy 600 eV; a collimation aperture of 2 micrometre width and
10 micrometre height placed 16.5 cm from the source; a double-slit 30.5 cm
beyond the collimation aperture, milled with a 30 keV Ga+ focused-ion-beam
system into a 100 nm silicon-nitride membrane coated with about 2 nm of gold,
with two slits of 50 nm width, 280 nm centre-to-centre separation and
4 micrometre height, each with a 150 nm support midway; a movable mask
5 micrometre wide, driven by a piezoelectric actuator and placed 230 micrometre
downstream of the double-slit; an electrostatic quadrupole lens magnifying the
pattern; and a two-dimensional microchannel plate and phosphor screen imaged by
a CCD camera. The body of the paper gives the mask height as 10 micrometre
while the caption of figure 1 gives 20 micrometre; the inconsistency is
recorded and not resolved here. The comparison is a reported experiment of the
framework in the sense of the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]; the identification of the
reported device with the quantities of any model's preparation or detection is
an apparatus identification carrying the source's limitations.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** The model assumes
that the **partition trace is strictly positive and finite**:
$$0<Z:=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta G}<\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}B:=\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\langle Bf,f\rangle$ for a
bounded positive $B$ and an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$, with value allowed
to be $+\infty$. Such a basis exists under the declared AC by the maximal
orthonormal-family argument using [[thm-zorn]] and the zero-complement
criterion of [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]].
This trace is basis independent: for $C:=B^{1/2}$ of
[[thm-positive-square-root]], the defining sum is
$\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\|Cf\|^2$, whose invariance is
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. When the sum is finite,
$C$ is Hilbert-Schmidt ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), so $B=C^2$ is
trace class by [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]],
and its ordinary trace is this same diagonal sum by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Apply this to the bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta G}$, since the
declared Gibbs generator $G$ is bounded below. The model
adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared model
at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta G}.$$
If the sector is zero-dimensional, its partition trace is $Z=0$, no
trace-one density exists, and no canonical density or equilibrium free
energy is assigned. On a nonzero finite-dimensional model space, $Z$ is a
positive finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues of $G$; no energy
sign restriction is needed. There $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]], and the
strict positivity and finiteness hypothesis is automatic. In reading (i),
$Z=Z_N$ and this is precisely the finite-sector Gibbs assignment.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the corresponding functional built from $G$.
Its physical Helmholtz free-energy reading applies in the stated finite
fixed-sector class; an effective-generator interpretation in a different
mode model is a separate declared reading. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

2.2 [Flow covariance] Define $W(t):=T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}$. It is a strongly continuous unitary group because $U_{V}$ is one and conjugation by the unitary $T_{a}$ preserves the group law, unitarity and strong continuity. For $x\in D(H_{V_{a}})=T_{a}D(H_{V})$ one has $T_{a}^{-1}x\in D(H_{V})$ and $\frac1t\bigl(W(t)x-x\bigr) =T_{a}\frac1t\bigl(U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}x-T_{a}^{-1}x\bigr) \longrightarrow T_{a}\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}x\Bigr) =-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{V_{a}}x,$ using the generator property of $U_{V}$ [F3] and step 1.3; the limit exists exactly on $D(H_{V_{a}})$ because the limit for $U_{V}$ exists exactly on $D(H_{V})$ [F3]. Hence $W$ is a strongly continuous unitary group with generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{V_{a}}$; by [F3] the group $t\mapsto U_{V_{a}}(t)=\exp(-itH_{V_{a}}/\hbar)$ has the same generator, and uniqueness of the group with a given generator gives $T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V_{a}}(t)$. If $V$ is invariant under translation by $a$ then $V_{a}=V$ almost everywhere and $T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V}$ with $T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V}(t)$; the free case $V=0$ is translation invariant for every $a$. This proves (c). [step 1.3, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

- **Sign of the shift.** The convention is that translating the preparation by
  $a$ moves the position law by $+a$: clause (b) says
  $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-a)$. Momentum laws are
  invariant because the translation commutes with $P_{k}$; this is the
  kinematic statement that translations are generated by momentum, and the
  generator identification itself is the mathematical content of
  [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (d).
- **What is not claimed.** No covariance of the internal factor under spatial
  transformations, no rotation or boost statement (those are separate items of
  this page), and no general covariance for potentials outside the bounded
  measurable class. The frame reading of clause (d) is a convention of the
  model and gains content only through the covariance statements (b) and (c).

$$Q\Psi_z=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt2}\bigl(a_\psi+a^\dagger_\psi\bigr)\Psi_z,\qquad P\Psi_z=\frac{\hbar}{i\ell\sqrt2}\bigl(a_\psi-a^\dagger_\psi\bigr)\Psi_z,$$
and the quadratic-form means and variances of the coherent vectors are
$$\langle Q\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\sqrt2\,\ell\operatorname{Re}z,\qquad\langle P\Psi_z,\Psi_z\rangle=\frac{\sqrt2\,\hbar}{\ell}\operatorname{Im}z,$$
$$\|(Q-\langle Q\rangle_zI)\Psi_z\|^{2}=\frac{\ell^{2}}{2},\qquad\|(P-\langle P\rangle_zI)\Psi_z\|^{2}=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\ell^{2}};$$

items.use_anchor: 4.1 [Energy variances] For the number state, $\|H_fUe_n\|^2=\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}$ by [F4], so the variance is $n(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2})$, which is strictly positive for $n\ge1$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]] (the energy multiplier has no eigenvalues, so $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}=\operatorname{Var}_\varphi(\varepsilon)>0$). For the coherent preparation, its Poisson second moment and [F1] give $U\psi_z\in D(H_f)$; the orthogonal-sector norm expansion therefore gives $$\|H_fU\psi_z\|^2=\sum_{n}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}\bigl(n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr)=x\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+x^{2}\bar\varepsilon^{2},$$ using the Poisson first and second factorial moments of step 2.1; subtracting the square of the mean $x\bar\varepsilon$ from step 3.1 gives $x\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}$, which is strictly positive for $x=|z|^{2}>0$ because $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}=\|\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi\|^{2}>0$: $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi$ vanishes only where $\varphi$ vanishes off the null set $\{k=0\}$, so a unit $\varphi$ cannot satisfy $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi=0$ in $\mathfrak h$. This proves (d). [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

  components, marker states and detector bin are declared apparatus data under
  P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). The composition
  assignment, the local readout convention and the marked model are adopted,
  not derived from the rest of the framework or from observation.
- **Derived results.** The conditional results of the page are the Schmidt
  reduction, purity criterion and exact pure separability/product equivalence for pure preparations
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-schmidt-reduction-and-pure-entanglement]]), the
  identification of local readout laws with the laws of the reduced
  preparation and its converse
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-readout-laws-and-reduced-preparations]]), the
  invariance of the untouched factor's reduced preparation under discarded
  local instruments, with the conditional reductions averaging back to it
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]]), and the
  contraction of the marker cross term with the visibility bound
  ([[pthm-nrqm-composites-marker-overlap-and-visibility-bound]]). Each is
  conditional on its stated hypotheses, including the choice hypotheses of the
  cited mathematics.
- **Empirical status.** No item of the page reports an experiment, a count, a
  calibration or a measured correlation, and none is a proof about nature. The
  detection weights and the visibility of the marked model are probabilities
  and contrasts of a declared model; whether a concrete interferometer
  realizes a marked model with particular components, marker states and bin is
  a tested identification with uncertainty in the sense of clauses (i)-(iii)
  of P7, and a comparison of the model with recorded data would require the
  sampling, efficiency, resolution and background qualifications of the
  apparatus, which this page does not supply.
- **Localized detections and accumulated distributions.** The detection
  weights of the page are probabilities for one trial of the declared model.
  An interference pattern is a property of the accumulated distribution of
  many detections, not of a single event, and a finite sample can fail a
  declared fringe criterion with positive probability under ordinary
  independent sampling even when the model is correct; nothing in the page
  draws a statistical conclusion from the displayed probabilities.
- **No-signalling is a model statement.** The invariance proved in
  [[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] is a statement
  about declared local instruments of the adopted framework and its
  mathematics. It is not a relativistic causality principle, does not assert
  anything about spacelike separation, and does not by itself exclude
  alternative models; the conditional changes of the measured factor's partner
  are the correlations of the model, and every interpretation of the
  alternatives, of the marker and of "which path" is outside the page.

  supplied or assumed here: setting-independent local-response models and the

  sectors and exclusion statements for identical particles; quantum circuits,
  teleportation and computation; and any dynamics, interaction or open-system
  model of decoherence, the marked model of this page being a kinematic
  preparation model.

items.use_anchor: **What is proved.** [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] identifies the atoms of the spectral measure with the eigenspace projections, so that an exact value has zero probability unless it is an eigenvalue. [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] identifies the support of the spectral measure with the spectrum, giving the precise reading of the statement that an outcome lies in the spectrum. [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] proves affinity under statistical mixtures and uniform trace-norm continuity. [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]] assembles the mean, second moment and variance formulas with their exact domain criteria, and [[lem-nrqm-observables-states-separated-by-bounded-projections]] proves that distinct states are separated by the law of a rank-one projection. The physics theorems read these results as conditional statements about assigned observables: [[pthm-nrqm-observables-born-outcome-law-properties]] (the law is a probability measure, affine in mixtures, atomic only at eigenvalues, supported in the spectrum and not assumed to have a density), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] (moments exist exactly under the stated domain hypotheses), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-position-and-momentum-outcome-laws]] (the position and momentum laws of the spinless massive model with densities $|\psi|^{2}$ and $|\mathcal F_2\psi|^{2}$, and the joint position measure) and [[pthm-nrqm-observables-states-separated-by-born-statistics]] (distinct preparations differ in some bounded observable's statistics).

[[ex-nrqm-potentials-rectangular-barrier-tunnelling-and-thick-limit]] treats
the rectangular barrier of [[pthm-nrqm-potentials-barrier-flux-and-transmission]]

value $1/25$ (the difference is exactly $-201/255025$) and verifies the

well depth at which the unique bound state is exactly solvable (even state,

generator_paragraphs:
**What is established.** The page fixes a declared effective one-dimensional
model of a spinless massive particle
([[def-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-line-model]]) and proves, as
conditional consequences of P1, P2, P4, P5 and the cited mathematics, the
following statements. The mathematical lemmas
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-free-operator-differential-identification]] and
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] identify the
free operator with the weak second-derivative operator and transfer
self-adjointness, resolvents, spectra and eigenfamilies along positive
scaling; [[lem-nrqm-potentials-one-dimensional-flux-identity]] proves the
one-dimensional continuity identity and the constancy of the current of a
stationary solution.
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-line-model-energy-and-stationary-states]] establishes
that the declared energy operator of the line model with a real bounded
measurable potential is an assigned sharp observable, generates the unitary
flow of the model, and that its stationary preparations are exactly the
eigenrays with point-mass energy law.
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-interval-spectra-completeness-and-nodes]] establishes,
for the declared Dirichlet and separated Robin interval models with continuous
real potentials, self-adjointness with compact resolvent, complete
orthonormal eigenbases, discreteness and simplicity of the spectra, the
min-max comparison of the Dirichlet energies with the free box energies and
the nodal counts, together with the Robin eigenvalue condition.
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-finite-well-bound-states]] gives the exact root
conditions, simplicity, parity and count of the bound states of the finite
square well, and
[[pthm-nrqm-potentials-delta-point-interaction-bound-state]] gives the
self-adjointness of the declared zero-range interface operator and its unique
bound state for attractive coupling with the exact energy
$-mg^{2}/(2\hbar^{2})$. [[pthm-nrqm-potentials-barrier-flux-and-transmission]]
gives the unique scattering solution of the rectangular barrier, its conserved
current, the exact coefficients $T$ and $R$, the flux balance $T+R=1$, the
reading of $T$ and $R$ as fractions of the reference current, and the
thick-barrier error bound.

- **Status of the examples.** Every item on this companion page is an
  idealised setup with a complete verification inside the declared model:
  the square well of
  [[ex-nrqm-scattering-square-well-s-wave-phase-shift]], the declared
  resonance factor of
  [[ex-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-cross-section]], the uniform
  ball Born amplitude of
  [[ex-nrqm-scattering-born-uniform-ball-amplitude]], and the Yukawa class
  check of
  [[ex-nrqm-scattering-long-range-tail-and-coulomb-warning]]. None is a
  reported experiment: there is no apparatus, calibration, sample, count or
  uncertainty budget on this page, and no number appearing here is a measured
  value.
- **Symbolic parameters.** The depth and radius of the well, the resonance
  energy and width, the ball strength and radius, and the Yukawa coupling and
  screening parameter remain symbolic throughout; the examples verify
  identities and class memberships, and assert no numerical value of $m$ or
  $\hbar$.
- **No extrapolation.** The hard-sphere comparison of the square-well example
  is a limit inside the declared family of wells; the low-energy limit is
  taken for the exact phase shift of the declared well and is not asserted as
  a universal low-energy law. The failures and limits recorded in the Yukawa
  example are statements about the declared potential class, not about any
  material target.

- **Long-range tails.** The short-range classes of
  [[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (b) exclude the
  pure Coulomb tail: the decaying-tail criterion of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]] clause (c)
  requires a positive power $\delta>0$, and the Coulomb quotient
  $(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}|V(x)|$ is unbounded for every $\delta>0$. The general resolvent-tail exclusion follows from clause (d) of that same theorem: its translated compact-bump input gives $h(r)\ge C/(2r+R)$ with $C>0$, which is not integrable. The Coulomb
  case is treated by the modified Dollard comparison
  ([[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]]), for which the ordinary
  short-range comparison is not claimed.
- **Threshold.** The completeness statements of this page are made for the
  declared classes and do not require a zero-energy nonresonance hypothesis
  ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-resolvent-tail-short-range-completeness]]).
  A different uniformity statement fails at zero energy: for compactly
  supported potentials the scattering defects are not compact uniformly when
  the energy cutoff does not vanish at $0$
  ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-compact-scattering-defects]]). The general stationary beam and amplitude theorems use $k>0$ and give no uniform zero-energy amplitude statement. The companion's declared square-well computation separately proves its explicit zero-energy resonance profile.
- **Positive eigenvalues.** The absence of positive eigenvalues is part of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]] clause
  (d) for the compact-support class; no statement is made about negative or
  zero eigenvalues of the interacting operator, and no general bound-state inventory belongs to this page. The companion's explicit well has a separately proved local threshold branch, without a bound-state count for arbitrary potentials.
- **Resonances.** The resonance model
  ([[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]]) is a declared
  conditional model; the page proves no existence of a resonance for any
  declared potential and makes no analytic-continuation claim for the
  resolvent or the scattering operator.

- *Model deductions.* The page proves, conditionally on the declared
  short-range model and the cited mathematics, the existence of the wave
  operators, their isometry and intertwining
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]]), the
  asymptotic completeness and unitarity of the scattering operator for the
  compact-support and resolvent-tail classes
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]],
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]]), the
  stationary outgoing solution with its amplitude and the cross-section
  readings ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]]), the controlled
  Born approximation with its operator-norm condition
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-controlled-born-approximation]]), the phase-shift
  cross-section series, the on-shell operator identification, and the
  conditional resonance-model algebra. Every one of these is a logical
  consequence of the stated postulates, model declarations, hypotheses and
  mathematics; none of them is an observation.
- *No observations.* The page reports no experiment: it contains no apparatus,
  no calibration, no sample, no count, no uncertainty budget and no measured
  cross section. Nothing on the page should be read as a measurement of $V$,
  $\kappa$, a phase shift or a resonance parameter.
- *What a comparison would require.* To compare the model quantities
  $d\sigma/d\Omega$ or $\sigma$ with data one needs a declared target
  preparation (target density and composition), an incident fluence with its
  own uncertainty, a stated scattering geometry, a detector acceptance and
  efficiency model, and a background model, together with a declared
  statistical model for the counts. The equal-channel elastic flux assumptions
  of the beam model ([[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]]
  clause (d)) must be justified for the particular apparatus; inelastic or
  multichannel processes lie outside the model and would require separate
  channels.
- *Interpretation.* Agreement of a measured count rate with the model reading
  is evidence for the combined model-plus-apparatus assumptions; it is not a
  deduction that the declared model, its potential class or the framework
  describes nature. Disagreement would not by itself falsify the whole
  framework, and a finite dataset can be compatible with a model without
  confirming it.

[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-free-translation-and-momentum]] is the exact free-model
computation: with $V\equiv0$ every translation is a symmetry, the free flow in
the momentum representation is the unimodular multiplier
$M_{f_{t}}$, $f_{t}(p)=e^{-it|p|^{2}/(2m\hbar)}$, the translations are the
multipliers $M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}}$, and the momentum components are
conserved sharp observables with the law, moment and generator statements of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]];
the modulus of the momentum representative is invariant in time almost
everywhere.
[[cex-nrqm-symmetries-nonconstant-potential-breaks-translation]] shows that
this fails as soon as the potential is nonconstant in the relevant direction:
for the bounded measurable indicator potential $1_{B(0,1)}$ no nonzero
translation is a symmetry, because the shifted potential differs from the
original on a set of positive measure, so the symmetry criterion of the
translation theorem is not met.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-parity-selection-rule]] derives, for a potential even
almost everywhere, that every energy eigenspace is invariant under the parity
action, that a nondegenerate eigenstate has definite parity, and that the
position matrix element of two states of equal parity vanishes.
[[ex-nrqm-symmetries-central-potential-rotation-invariance]] verifies the
almost-everywhere rotational and parity invariance of a bounded radial
potential and instantiates
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]]: all rotations are
symmetries, the rotation action is a strongly continuous unitary symmetry
group, and the coordinate-rotation generators $L_{i}$ are conserved sharp
observables, with the underlying conservation mechanism of
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]].

The items of this page are conditional consequences of the framework's
postulates and of the cited mathematics.
[[def-nrqm-symmetries-framework-symmetry-groups-and-conservation]] fixes the
vocabulary: a symmetry of the declared dynamics is a unitary preserving the
energy domain and commuting with the energy operator, a unitary symmetry group
is a group of such symmetries, a conserved sharp observable is one whose
outcome law is time-independent in every preparation, and the translations,
spatial rotations, parity and gauge multipliers are recorded as the model's
candidate actions, not as symmetries.
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-unitary-conjugation-and-commutation-calculus]] proves the
equivalence between flow commutation, strong spectral commutation and domain
invariance of a self-adjoint observable;
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-parity-action]],
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-rotation-generators-on-schwartz-classes]] and
[[lem-nrqm-symmetries-free-flow-multiplier-form]] provide the concrete actions
and their operator identities on the component-valued model.
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-generator-conservation]] proves the equivalence of the
commutation conditions with the conservation of the outcome law and the
conservation of moments, and covers self-adjoint unitary symmetries;
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-translation-invariance-and-momentum-conservation]]
decides exactly which bounded potentials have the translations as symmetries
and derives momentum conservation for the translation-invariant case;
[[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-rotational-and-parity-invariance]] does the same for
rotations (with conservation of the coordinate-rotation generators) and for
parity; and [[pthm-nrqm-symmetries-gauge-covariance]] transports the
prescribed-coupling operator under gauge transformations of
[[post-nrqm-symmetries-prescribed-external-coupling]], exhibits the exact
criterion under which a gauge multiplier is a symmetry of the fixed dynamics
and identifies the global-phase case. Every one of these statements is
conditional on P1, P2, P4, P5, P5a and P6 in their stated readings, on the
choice assumptions displayed with the items, and on the cited operator
analysis.

**No conflation.** The Robertson relation bounds the product of two
preparation spreads; it does not bound an apparatus error, it does not bound a
disturbance, and it is not a statement that measuring one quantity "must"
perturb another by a fixed amount. The heuristic accounts of measurement
intrusion in the literature are accordingly used on this page at most as
motivation: the exact statements are the preparation-spread results, and the
identification of a concrete apparatus with a declared instrument is a tested
identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate
P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

items.use_anchor: 4.1 [Why the comparison does not discriminate and what would] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 show equality of the two declared normalised two-bin laws for every datum; the equality of one class of predictions of two distinct models is not evidence for either, and it does not establish field quantisation. The models differ in their objects and in their assignments elsewhere: the classical model carries a deterministic intensity and no count law, whereas the quantised model assigns the sharp count law of a number state and the Poisson law of a coherent state under the declared number detector ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] clauses (a),(b)). A discriminating comparison must therefore be designed on a prediction where the two declared models differ, with the detector response, preparation and sampling model declared in the sense of [F5]; no such comparison is constructed here and no data is reported. This proves (c) and (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F5] ∎

generator_paragraphs: 1.2 [Radial form proof of zero exclusion] Define $S_su(r)=e^{s/2}u(e^sr)$ for real $s$. Change of variables gives unitarity on $L^2$, preservation of $V_l$, and on the smooth form core the exact identity $a_l(S_su,v)=e^{2s}a_l(u,S_{-s}v)+\gamma(e^{2s}-e^s)\langle S_s(u/r),v\rangle$. Kinetic and angular terms scale by $e^{2s}$ and the Coulomb term by $e^s$. Continuity extends the identity to all $u,v\in V_l$, since $u/r\in L^2$. If $u\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lu=0$, the form criterion gives $S_su\in D(A_l)$ and $A_lS_su=\gamma(e^{2s}-e^s)S_s(u/r)$. Self-adjointness yields $0=\langle A_lS_su,u\rangle=\gamma(e^{2s}-e^s)\langle S_s(u/r),u\rangle$. For $\gamma>0$ and $s\ne0$ divide by the nonzero coefficient. Strong continuity $S_sh\to h$ follows first for compact continuous $h$ by dominated convergence and then by density and unitarity for all $h\in L^2$. Letting $s\to0$ gives $\int|u|^2/r=0$, hence $u=0$. For $\gamma=0$, $0=\langle A_lu,u\rangle=\|u'-u/r\|_2^2+l(l+1)\|u/r\|_2^2$; the identity $\|u'-u/r\|_2=\|u'\|_2$ extends from the form core to $V_l$, so $u'=0$ and its $L^2$ constant representative is zero. No unbounded dilation generator is differentiated. [F1, F3, F4, given, algebra]

7.1 [Borel density without a regularity prerequisite] For $0<a<b$, continuous $h_n(E)=\min(1,n(E-a)_+,n(b-E)_+)$ increase to $\mathbf1_{(a,b)}$ and vanish outside $[a,b]$. Step 6.1 and dominated convergence give $\mu_g((a,b))=\int_a^b d_g(E)dE$. Every positive singleton has zero mass by shrinking intervals around it and local boundedness of $d_g$. On a fixed compact interval $[c,d]\subset(0,\infty)$, the two finite measures agree on all subintervals, including endpoints. Agreement on every relative Borel set follows by the elementary measure uniqueness argument: agreement sets form a Dynkin class (equal total mass, relative complements, disjoint countable unions), and intervals form an intersection-stable generator. For completeness, let $\mathcal D$ be the smallest Dynkin class containing these intervals and the full compact interval; for a fixed generating interval $I$, the sets $B$ with $I\cap B\in\mathcal D$ form a Dynkin class containing the generators, hence contain $\mathcal D$. Repeating this with any fixed $B\in\mathcal D$ shows that $\mathcal D$ is closed under intersections of its members. A Dynkin class closed under intersections is a sigma algebra by disjointifying countable unions, so it contains the generated Borel sigma algebra. Exhaustion by $[1/n,n]$ proves equality on every positive Borel set. The same exhaustion bounds the total density integral by $\|g\|^2$. This proves density before either Stone's interval formula or an onto transform, without a separate finite-measure regularity assumption. [step 6.1, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [(b) generator and its exact domain] Let $f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ and $g_t:=\frac1t(U(t)f-f)+\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}f=\sum_n\varepsilon_n(t)c_n\psi_n$ with $\varepsilon_n(t)=\frac{e^{-i\omega(n+1/2)t}-1}{t}+i\omega(n+\frac12)$. Hence $t\mapsto U(t)f$ is differentiable at $0$ with derivative $-\frac{i}{\hbar}H_{\mathrm{osc}}f$; the general $t$ follows from the group law and $U(t)f\in D(H_{\mathrm{osc}})$ (the coefficients $e^{-i\omega(n+1/2)t}c_n$ have the same moduli as $c_n$).
